label: Squarish-shell 3BR / baths DISTRIBUTED (two dispersed common baths, no ensuite), HALF-SPINE — one bedroom+bath pair is served by a real hall spine, the other bedroom+bath pair sits directly off the great_room behind a short buffer. Sourced from pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1, whose defining move is splitting the private zone's circulation logic in two: half hall-served, half open straight onto the LDK.

adjacencies.note: great_room + kitchen form the open LDK (gr style), matching the source's continuous LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN volume

the east hall's mouth opens into the great_room. FIXED from the source: pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1 doors this connection off a single hinged door (flagged 'violated' against the rule 2 [PREFER] hallway-open-to-public default); this topology applies the catalog's standard open-mouth convention instead.
master (the source's largest, undesignated BEDROOM 1) doors into the east hall, at its front end
br2 doors into the east hall, at its rear end — matches the source's BEDROOM 2
east wing's shared bath doors into the hall, between master and br2 — matches the source's T&B between BEDROOM 2 and BEDROOM 1
geometry only, no door — matches the source's T&B/BEDROOM 1 shared wall
geometry only, no door — matches the source's BEDROOM 2/T&B shared wall

br3 doors directly onto the great_room — the half of the plan with NO dedicated hall, matching the source's BEDROOM 3 (which opens straight onto the open LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN volume with no hallway on that side of the plan at all). Kept as-is per rule 1's sanctioned tight-lot-bedroom-off-public exception, rather than forcing a hall this precedent never had.
a short buffer/vestibule opens off the great_room, sized only to host common_w's door

west bath doors into the small vestibule. FIXED from the source: pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1's T&B (under BEDROOM 3) opens with no vestibule at all straight onto the open LIVING/DINING/KITCHEN volume, in view of the sofa and dining table (flagged 'violated' against rule 1's 'bath opens off circulation, not public' spirit — the same category of finding as pep_SHD-2015021's guest bath). Unlike br3's direct public door (a sanctioned bedroom exception), a bath with no buffer at all has no such exception, so this topology gives it the smallest workable vestibule rather than leaving it on the open floor.
geometry only, no door — matches the source's BEDROOM 3/T&B shared wall

soft_proximities.note: mild pull to keep both wing entries reasonably aligned along the great_room's rear wall

lot_adjustment_profiles.name: compact_sq_half_spine_baths_ds_hall_gr
lot_adjustment_profiles.rationale: Half the private zone pays for a hall (east wing) while the other half (west wing) only pays for a small bath vestibule, so this parti is cheaper on circulation than a full side_split or center_spine but pricier than the source's own no-vestibule version. Profile triggers at 105 m², matching the source's generous 146 m² footprint at the high end and giving room to relax down toward a tighter squarish shell before falling back.

notes: Squarish 3BR catalog topology — HALF-SPINE, first squarish member of the
half_spine family (the wide sibling, 1s_3br_wd_half_spine_baths_ds_hall_lk,
uses 'half' in a different sense — there, the ENTIRE private zone is
hall-served and 'half' refers to which half of the FOOTPRINT carries the
spine at all. Here, sourced from pep_SHD-2017036-DESIGN1, both halves of
the footprint hold private rooms, but only one wing's bedroom+bath pair is
hall-served — the other wing's pair opens directly onto the great_room.
Both readings share the token because both leave exactly half the private
program without dedicated circulation; the source record's own
parti_note makes the same call.
Layout intent (canonical, hall-served wing on the right):
Right (spine) wing: [master (front) | hall_e | br2 : common_e (rear)]
Center:             [great_room (entry, front) | kitchen (rear)]
Left (open) wing:   [br3 (doors to great) : common_w (vestibule only)]
No bedroom is designated master in the source (all three carry plain
numbers). master here is the source's largest and hall-served BEDROOM 1
(18.0 sqm) — a judgement call on size and hall position alone, consistent
with how this project resolves undesignated-master precedents elsewhere.
Two corrections made from the source, per established catalog practice of
fixing access/privacy issues found in source drawings when authoring the
canonical form:
1. hall_e <-> great is open_plan here; the source doors this connection
with a single hinged door (a rule 2 [PREFER] violation the source's
own compliance notes flag).
2. common_w gets a minimal vestibule (hall_w) rather than opening with no
buffer at all onto the open LDK, as the source's T&B does (flagged in
the source as a rule 1 [PREFER] violation with 'no stated layout win'
justifying it).
Preserved as-is: br3's direct bedroom_to_public door. This is the sanctioned
tight-lot exception (rule 1), not the same category of issue as an
un-buffered bath door, and it is the defining feature that makes this a
genuinely half-spine parti rather than a relabelled side_split.
Wet core: fully dispersed, matching the source (the two baths share no wall
with each other or the kitchen) — grade 'dispersed' per rule 3, accepted
here as in the source rather than invented as a fix, since clustering would
require relocating a whole wing.
Carport: NCP base form. The source shows an open (unwalled) carport eating
most of one side setback; declare via brief.carport_side rather than baking
it into the base topology, per catalog convention.
STATUS: NOT VALIDATED — structurally unworkable as specified. Full
re-authoring attempt 2026-08-12; findings below so it is not redone.
The authoring-time claim of 'a reproducible, environment-specific solver
issue' was WRONG and is removed. Two real defects, one fatal.
1. OVER-CONSTRAINED ANCHORS (fixable). left_anchored + right_anchored
declared together are infeasible at any lot — the trap CLAUDE.md records
from 2026-07-19. Bisected at 25x25: either list alone still fails, both
dropped solves. Room-level bisection found no lighter fix: removing any
single room from either list, or one room from each, still fails.
2. THE WEST WING CANNOT HOLD ITS WIDTH (fatal as designed). `great` must
touch kitchen, hall_e, br3 AND hall_w, so it wraps the west wing rather
than sitting beside it, and there is nothing to stop it swallowing that
side. The single feasible configuration (both anchor lists null) gives at
15x15: great 50.6 and master 32.2 against kitchen 3.5, br2/br3 at the
6.0 m2 PD 1096 hard floor, common_w 2.0 and hall_w 1.5. The east wing is
fine; only the west collapses.
This topology's own lot_adjustment_profiles would fix the sizes — it caps
master at 15.0 and bedroom_standard at 12.0 — but it is DEAD CODE: it
fires below 105 m2 buildable and the topology is infeasible below 15x15
(120 m2 buildable), so it can never trigger. Raising the threshold to 130
makes the solve INFEASIBLE, and per-cap bisection shows why: `common_bath
min_area 3.0` and `hallway min_least_dim 0.95` are individually
unsatisfiable. common_w cannot reach 3 m2 and hall_w cannot reach 0.95 m
wide. A bath under 3 m2 is the defect, not the cap.
Also tried and infeasible: three clean front_to_rear_stacks columns matching
the layout intent above; zone_split nulled (it was wrong anyway — it declares
private_side 'right' while listing only the east rooms, though br3/common_w/
hall_w are private and sit west); match_bedroom_widths; keeping left_anchored
alone or right_anchored alone; and every combination of those with the caps.
set_max_area_sqm does not help either, because snap_gaps and the dead-strip
claimer inflate rooms AFTER the solve.
TO PROCEED, the ROOM PROGRAM has to change — a design decision, not tuning.
The blocker is that hall_w and common_w are squeezed between br3 and a
great_room that must also reach hall_e and kitchen. Options: drop hall_w and
re-buffer common_w some other way (but the vestibule was itself a deliberate
correction to the source's un-buffered bath door); move common_w into the
east wing (but then it is not a half-spine); or give the west wing a real
column the great_room cannot wrap.
